Cait's California Registration

Prep for Lori's meeting with Cait Townsley. How to register her New Mexico company in California so DOJ can approve her, what it costs, how long it takes, and every bizfile screen she'll see.

The Fix
Why DOJ said no. Her business has to be registered with the California Secretary of State. It's the only reason checked on her denial letter.
What she does. Registers her existing New Mexico company in California as an out-of-state company. She keeps it exactly as it is.
Then. Files a Statement of Information and reapplies to DOJ with proof.
Confirmed. Her work doesn't require a California license, so she's clear to register this way.
One-time fees$122New Mexico certificate, registration, certified copy, Statement of Information
Every year$800California tax, plus a registered agent ($0 to about $300)
First $800 dueAt registrationIf she registers in 2026. See Step 3.
Approval2–4business days, standard (Lori's estimate). Rush options cost extra.

Questions to ask Cait

For Lori
  • What's her company's exact legal name, and is it in good standing in New Mexico? A missed New Mexico filing means no certificate.
  • Does she use a different name with clients than her legal company name? If so, she may also need a Fictitious Business Name in California after registering.
  • Who will be her registered agent? Meg (only if Meg is comfortable), another California resident she knows, or a paid service.
  • Does she have a tax preparer who can file a California return?
  • How fast does she need DOJ approval? That decides between filing now, a future effective date or January, and whether to pay for a rush.

Step by Step

Eight steps from the New Mexico certificate to DOJ approval. Step 4 walks through every bizfile screen.

1

Order a New Mexico Certificate of Good Standing

$26.95 · Ready instantly

Official proof that her New Mexico company is active and current. California won't accept her registration without it.

IMPORTANT: It must be dated within six months of the day she files in California, and saved as a PDF. If her New Mexico company has a missed filing, she has to fix that first.

2

Choose a California registered agent

$0 to about $300 per year · Must be in place before Step 4

California calls this an "agent for service of process." It's the person or company that accepts lawsuits, legal notices and official state mail for her business in California and passes them to her.

Why it's required. bizfile asks for the agent's name and California street address, and won't let her continue without one.

Who can serve. Any adult living in California with a physical California street address, or a registered agent company approved by California. Cait can't serve herself because she lives outside California.

Option A · Meg

Free · Only if Meg is comfortable with it

  • Meg's name and street address become public record
  • She'd accept lawsuits, legal notices and record requests for Cait's business and forward them right away
  • Get her agreement in writing (an email is fine)
  • Nothing for Meg to file

Option B · Someone else Cait knows

Free

  • Must live in California
  • Same responsibilities as Meg
  • Get their agreement in writing

Option C · A paid service

About $50 to $300 per year · Sign-up takes minutes

  • Keeps a private person's address off the public record
  • She must sign up and get approval before naming the service in bizfile
  • She enters the company's name exactly as California lists it

Where to find one. California's official list is built into bizfile. On the agent screen, she chooses California Registered Corporate Agent (1505) and clicks Search for an alphabetical list of approved companies. A few well-known ones:

  • California Corporate Agents · about $50 a year
  • Harbor Compliance · about $99 a year
  • CorpNet · about $149 a year
  • Northwest Registered Agent

Prices are from each company's site and can change. These are examples, not recommendations.

If the agent changes later. She updates it online with a Statement of Information. An agent who wants out can file a free resignation form.

3

Decide when the registration takes effect

$800 per year · Decide before Step 4

Every Limited Liability Company registered in California owes $800 a year, whatever it earns, and there's no free first year anymore. When the first payment is due depends on her company's tax year and when her registration takes effect.

Why the first $800 is due right away

Tax year timing
  1. Her tax year runs January 1 to December 31. That's the standard calendar tax year most small companies use. Her tax professional can confirm hers.
  2. California's normal due date is the 15th day of the 4th month of the tax year. For a calendar year, that's April 15.
  3. A brand-new California company gets about three and a half months. Its clock starts the day it forms. That's the window most people have heard about.
  4. Cait's company isn't new. It's an existing out-of-state company, and its 2026 tax year started back in January. California's rule for that case is that if it registers after the April 15 cutoff, the tax is due as soon as it registers (or as soon as it starts doing business in California, whichever comes first).
  5. So registering in November 2026 means paying for 2026 right away. Then her 2027 tax year starts January 1, and that $800 is due April 15, 2027.
  6. A January effective date flips it. Her registration would start in the 2027 tax year, before the April 15 cutoff, so the normal April 15, 2027 due date applies and there's no 2026 payment.

The rule is on the Franchise Tax Board's Limited Liability Company filing information page, under "Due Dates for First-Year Annual Tax Payment."

Pick an option to see what it means for her.

Upfront
$800 payments by April 15, 2027
DOJ reapplication

Confirm with a tax professional before choosing. For the future effective date option, the tax professional should confirm the Franchise Tax Board treats the January effective date as her registration date.
4

File the registration on bizfile Online

$75 with the certified copy · About 20 minutes · 2–4 business days for approval

The official California registration. In bizfile she chooses Forms, then Registration – Out-of-State LLC. It's online only, and there are eleven screens. The walkthrough below shows each one.

IMPORTANT: Fees aren't refunded if the filing is rejected, so she should have everything from the checklist ready. She can click Save Draft on any screen and come back later.

A red X beside a screen name in bizfile just means that screen still has something missing. These screenshots were taken while testing, so some show red X marks and a blurred sample address.

5

Pay the $800 tax

$800 · Due when she registers if it takes effect in 2026, or by April 15, 2027

California's yearly Limited Liability Company tax, paid to the Franchise Tax Board (California's tax agency), not the Secretary of State. bizfile doesn't collect it, so this is a separate payment after her registration is approved.

How to pay online

Franchise Tax Board
  1. Go to ftb.ca.gov/pay and choose Web Pay for Businesses (pay from a bank account). The first time, she sets up a free account.
  2. Entity type is Limited Liability Company.
  3. Enter her California entity number. That's the file number on her approved registration, which she can find in bizfile under My Records.
  4. Payment type is LLC Tax Voucher (Form 3522).
  5. Pick the tax year. That's 2026 for the payment due at registration and 2027 for the April 15, 2027 payment.
  6. Enter $800, pay and save the confirmation.

Good to know. Web Pay lets her schedule a payment up to a year ahead, so she can set up the April 15, 2027 payment at the same time. She can pay by credit card instead through the Franchise Tax Board's card processor, but that adds a convenience fee. Paying online means she doesn't mail the paper Form 3522.

IMPORTANT: The tax is still owed for any year she's registered, even if she earns nothing in California. A separate income-based fee only applies if her California income reaches $250,000.

6

File the Statement of Information

$20 · Right after approval, takes about 5 minutes

A short online form confirming her business details and registered agent. California requires it within 90 days, and our COR tracker notes it's a document DOJ wants to see, so she should file it the same day she's approved. She'll repeat it every two years.

IMPORTANT: Missing the deadline means a $250 penalty and possible suspension of her California registration.

7

Reapply to DOJ

No extra cost · Same day as Step 6

Her denial letter says she can reapply once she completes registration with the California Secretary of State. Per our COR tracker, she replies on her existing DOJ email thread (authorizationquestions@doj.ca.gov) and attaches the items below.

  • Everything the denial letter listed
  • The certified copy of her approved registration (from My Work Queue in bizfile)
  • Her filed Statement of Information
  • Her Fictitious Business Name, only if she does business under a different name

IMPORTANT: With a future effective date, her registration isn't official until that date, so she can't send proof to DOJ before then.

For the meeting

Lori's Questions

  1. California registration fee. $70, plus $5 for the certified copy DOJ needs (Step 4).
  2. New Mexico Certificate of Good Standing fee. $25 plus a $1.95 online fee (Step 1).
  3. California registered agent cost. $0 if a California resident she knows will serve, otherwise about $50 to $300 a year (Step 2).
  4. Statement of Information fee. $20, filed right after approval and then every two years (Step 6).
  5. The $800 annual tax. Due right when she registers if it takes effect in 2026. By April 15, 2027 if it takes effect in January. Then every April 15. No first-year exemption (Step 3).
  6. Other required filing, publication or administrative costs. No publication is required. There's the yearly California tax return (Form 568) and preparer fees, optional rush fees, and an income-based fee only at $250,000 or more.
  7. Totals. About $922 to $1,222 upfront if she files now, or $122 to $422 with a January effective date or a January filing. Plus $800 by April 15, 2027. Ongoing, about $810 to $1,110 a year plus tax preparation.

Can Cait keep her New Mexico company? Yes. This is an out-of-state registration. Her company stays a New Mexico company that's also authorized in California.

Will this give DOJ what they asked for? Yes. Her denial letter says that once she completes registration with the California Secretary of State, she may reapply and submit proof.

For the meeting

Cait's Questions

Tap a question to open it.

Do I need to form a new company?

No. She registers her existing New Mexico company to do business in California.

Can I file a Fictitious Business Name like Jackson did?

No. California counties won't accept a Fictitious Business Name for a Limited Liability Company that isn't registered with the Secretary of State first, so it doesn't skip any steps or costs.

Do I need a California address?

Only for her registered agent. Her business address is her New Mexico address.

What will be public?

Everything she enters, including names, phone numbers, email addresses and every address. It can show up in search engines and stays public even if she later cancels. Only payment details stay private.

Why do I owe $800 if I barely earn anything in California?

The tax applies to every Limited Liability Company registered in California, whatever its income. It's a cost of being registered, not a tax on profit.

Why is the first $800 due right away?

Because her company already exists and its 2026 tax year started in January. Brand-new California companies get about three and a half months, but an existing out-of-state company registering after mid-April pays when it registers.

What if the filing is rejected?

Fees aren't refunded, and a rush fee doesn't carry over to a resubmission. bizfile will say what to fix. The most common problems are a name that doesn't match the certificate or a missing PDF.

Can I save my progress?

Yes. Every bizfile screen has a Save Draft button.

What if DOJ denies me again after I register?

The $800 is still owed for any year she's registered. Registration fixes the only reason DOJ listed, so this risk is low.

What if I stop working with California families later?

She can cancel her California registration online for free with a Certificate of Cancellation. That stops future $800 payments. She should confirm what's owed for the final year with a tax professional.

Will California tax my income?

Possibly, on income that comes from California. That's a question for her tax professional.

Do I need a lawyer?

No. Most business owners file this themselves. The Secretary of State does suggest talking to one before filing if she has questions about her situation.

Who can I call with bizfile questions?

California Secretary of State customer service at (916) 657-5448.

Does any of this change my New Mexico company?

No. She just keeps her New Mexico filings current so she stays in good standing in both states.

For Cait to confirm with a tax professional

Before filing
  • Whether a January effective date or a January filing avoids the 2026 tax in her situation
  • How California taxes the income she earns from California families and schools
  • Who will prepare and file her California tax return (Form 568) each year
